about: Fire code and ERCES rule by state. A lead, not an answer: the AHJ confirms it. status says how far each was read. Built by tools/build_state_rules.py.

labels.no_mandate: No mandate: state law bars requiring one

AK.name: Alaska

fire_code.base: IFC
fire_code.effective: Search summary: new Title 13 AAC 50-55 codes took effect 2022-10-28 (not seen in the rule text)
fire_code.statewide: yes (State Fire Marshal / Division of Fire and Life Safety); local enforcement not verified
fire_code.state_amendments: 13 AAC 50.025 (IFC 2021 Ch.1-12, 20-40, 50-67, 80 and Appendices B-1, K, L, N adopted; Ch.13-19, 41-49, 68-79 reserved) - Chapter 5 incl. Sec. 510 is inside the adopted chapters

erces.citation: IFC 2021 Sec. 510 via 13 AAC 50.025
erces.summary: No Alaska amendment to Section 510 seen. One amendment lets the fire department require emergency responder radio coverage alongside access roads, hydrants and key boxes, and requires documentation that the fire chief was consulted.

AK.ahj: State Fire Marshal (Dept. of Public Safety, Division of Fire and Life Safety) for plan review; local fire chiefs where they exist.

AL.name: Alabama

fire_code.base: IFC

fire_code.statewide: yes (State Fire Marshal rule); many cities also adopt locally - not verified
fire_code.state_amendments: Ala. Admin. Code 482-2-101-.02 (IFC 2021 with Appendices B,C,D,E,M adopted; Part 2 of Ch.1 and Appendices A,F-L not adopted; D107 and 1103.5.4/App. M recommended only)

erces.citation: IFC 2021 Sec. 510 (via Ala. Admin. Code 482-2-101-.02)
erces.summary: The state rule adopts the IFC 2021 and its exclusion list does not touch Chapter 5 or Section 510, so the model-code ERCES requirement stands as written. We did not open the model Section 510 text this session.
erces.thresholds: Model-code triggers (new buildings; existing per Ch.11) - not read

AL.local_amendments: Not verified. The state rule is used for projects under State Fire Marshal review; Rule 482-2-101-.05 lets the State Fire Marshal allow later editions per project.
AL.ahj: State Fire Marshal (Alabama Department of Insurance) for state-reviewed projects; local fire officials elsewhere - split not verified.
AL.pending: None found (no 2025-2026 Alabama ERCES bill turned up in searches).

AR.name: Arkansas

fire_code.base: IFC (as Arkansas Fire Prevention Code)
fire_code.effective: 2023-01-01 (adopted Ark. Register Vol. 47 No. 07, effective 7/1/2022 per LII notes)
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: 2021 Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 015.01.22 Ark. Code R. 005 (Arkansas State Police rules; Vol. I Fire)

erces.citation: IFC 2021 Sec. 510, 1103.2, 105.6.4 (Arkansas Fire Prevention Code Vol. I)
erces.summary: The Arkansas amendments text we read has no change to Section 510, so the IFC 2021 requirement stands: approved in-building coverage in new buildings unless the fire code official finds it not needed; existing buildings via Chapter 11. AR.ahj: Arkansas State Fire Marshal (Director of the Arkansas State Police by law); local fire officials enforce locally - split not verified.
AR.pending: None found. No 2024 Arkansas edition found.

AZ.name: Arizona

fire_code.base: IFC (state fire code); local codes govern most buildings
fire_code.edition: State: IFC 2024 per a search summary of the OSFM page (April 2026); locals vary (Phoenix 2024 IFC; one fire authority on 2018 IFC with 2020 amendments)
fire_code.effective: not confirmed
fire_code.statewide: partial: state fire code applies to state and county buildings, schools, and areas with no local fire code; cities and fire districts adopt their own
fire_code.state_amendments: Arizona Administrative Code Title 4, Ch. 36 (State Fire Code, incorporates IFC by reference with Article 3 changes) - text not opened

erces.citation: none statewide found; local IFC Sec. 510 amendments
erces.summary: No Arizona statute or state rule found requiring or banning ERCES. Whether Section 510 applies depends on the local fire code a city or fire district adopted. The AZ Secretary of State rules site returned a bot-check page, so Title 4 Ch. 36 was not read and we did not work around it.

AZ.local_amendments: Yes: cities, counties and fire districts adopt and amend their own fire codes (search summary). Cited statutes A.R.S. 9-808 and 11-861 were not opened.
AZ.ahj: Local fire code official; Office of the State Fire Marshal for state/county buildings, schools, and unincorporated areas without a local code.
AZ.pending: HB 2324 (2026, signed 2026-04-13, 'Fire Marshal Bill Burns Act') concerns municipal fire inspection reports and county building inventory - not ERCES. No ERCES bill found.

CA.name: California

fire_code.base: IFC (as California Fire Code, Title 24 Part 9)
fire_code.edition: 2025 CFC (based on IFC 2024)
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: California Code of Regulations Title 24 Part 9, adopted via Title 19 Div 1; state amendments by State Fire Marshal / Building Standards Commission

erces.citation: 2025 CFC Sec. 510 (Emergency Responder Communications Enhancement Systems), 510.5.5
erces.summary: Section 510 is in the statewide code. California adds language letting the fire code official accept an automatically activated coverage system where a required system could disturb normal facility operations. Local jurisdictions amend 510 freely (Corona requires ERCES in all new buildings based on exterior public safety coverage; San Francisco amends it too).
erces.thresholds: Model-code triggers plus local amendments; test 95% per floor

CA.local_amendments: Yes: cities and counties adopt local amendments (Corona 15.12.250 amends 510.1; SF Fire Code 2025). The state statute that governs this (H&S Code 17958.7 findings) was not opened.
CA.ahj: Local fire code official; State Fire Marshal for state-owned buildings, schools, and certain institutional occupancies.

CO.name: Colorado

fire_code.base: none statewide for general buildings; IFC by local adoption
fire_code.edition: State DFPC: IFC editions for schools, junior colleges and licensed health care (editions disagree between sources: 2012, 2021, 2024); Denver 2025 Denver Fire Code amends IFC 2024
fire_code.effective: Denver: 2025 amendments (June 2025, 2nd printing Nov 2025)
fire_code.statewide: no, local adoption (home rule)
fire_code.state_amendments: Division of Fire Prevention and Control rules for state-scope buildings; Denver Fire Code 2025 for Denver

erces.citation: Denver Fire Code 2025 Sec. 510 (local); no state ERCES statute found
erces.summary: Colorado leaves ERCES to local fire codes. Read for Denver: 2025 Denver Fire Code replaces 510.1 so coverage is required for high-rise, underground and airport buildings, plus new buildings that must be tested at completion; failing buildings get an ERCES; retest every 5 years under DFD Policy 510-1.
erces.thresholds: Denver 510.1.1 test triggers: Type I/II over 50,000 gross sq ft; Group E and I over 12,000 sq ft on any story; Type III/IV/V over 100,000 sq ft with masonry shafts/walls/floors; occupiable below-grade area over 10,000 sq ft

CO.local_amendments: Yes, home rule: cities and counties adopt and amend (Denver, Aurora, Colorado Springs, Fort Collins, Boulder named in summaries). State statute not opened.
CO.ahj: Local fire marshal / fire code official; DFPC where no local program exists and for schools and licensed health care.
CO.pending: None found. Colorado bills seen (SB25-031, HB26-1238, HB26-1252) are not about in-building coverage. Note: the 'read' status on erces covers Denver only; the state-level finding is an excerpt.

CT.name: Connecticut

fire_code.base: two codes: NFPA 1 (State Fire Prevention Code) and IFC (State Fire Safety Code Part III)
fire_code.edition: NFPA 1 2021 and IFC 2021 (2022 Connecticut State Fire Prevention Code and 2022 State Fire Safety Code); errata #1 dated 2023-04-12
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: 2022 Connecticut State Fire Prevention Code (NFPA 1 amendments) and 2022 Connecticut State Fire Safety Code (IFC amendments)

erces.citation: CSFSC 2022 IFC Sec. 510.1 (model), amended 510.2 and added 102.1.1.1; CSFPC NFPA 1 Sec. 11.10
erces.summary: IFC 510.1 for new buildings is kept; Connecticut amends 510.2 so existing buildings other than R-3 that are undergoing an addition, alteration, renovation or change of use and lack approved coverage must get it, on a time frame set by the adopting authority. Exception where the fire code official finds a system is not needed. In the NFPA 1 code, 11.10 is replaced: installed systems only need to be maintained per NFPA 1221.
erces.thresholds: Existing non-R-3 buildings on addition/alteration/change of use; new buildings per IFC 510.1

CT.local_amendments: Not verified. Source says the State Fire Marshal is the AHJ for administration, interpretation and modification; local fire marshal makes the initial compliance determination.
CT.ahj: State Fire Marshal administers the codes; local fire marshals do the initial determination and inspections.

DC.name: District of Columbia

fire_code.base: IFC (DC Fire Code, 12-H DCMR)
fire_code.edition: IFC 2021 base with DC amendments (2023 DC Construction Codes) - edition not confirmed from DC's own page
fire_code.effective: not confirmed
fire_code.statewide: yes (single jurisdiction)
fire_code.state_amendments: 12 DCMR Subtitle H (Fire Code Supplement); Chapter 12-H5 includes 12-H510 'Emergency Responder Radio Coverage'

erces.citation: 12 DCMR 12-H510 and 12-H1103 (older 2013 supplement text only)
erces.summary: DC amends IFC for existing buildings: those lacking approved coverage, based on District public safety system levels at the exterior, must be equipped within a time frame set by the Office of Unified Communications and the fire code official, unless they decide it is not needed. This is from the 2013 supplement as quoted by a code site; the current 2023 text was not found.

DC.local_amendments: Not applicable (single government); DC amends the IFC itself.
DC.ahj: DC Fire and EMS Department (Fire Marshal) enforces the Fire Code; DC DOB issues permits.

DE.name: Delaware

fire_code.base: NFPA 1 (with NFPA 101); Delaware has no statewide IFC
fire_code.edition: NFPA 1 2024, NFPA 101 2024 (Delaware State Fire Prevention Regulations, Reg. 701)
fire_code.effective: 2026-01-01 (projects submitted on or after 2025-12-31 use the 2026 edition)
fire_code.statewide: yes (State Fire Prevention Commission regulations); building-code enforcement is local
fire_code.state_amendments: Delaware State Fire Prevention Regulations (1 DE Admin Code 701; NFPA codes adopted in entirety except listed changes)

erces.citation: NFPA 1 2024 Sec. 11.10 (not opened); 1 DE Admin Code 702 (high-rise)
erces.summary: No Delaware amendment to ERCES found. For high-rise buildings, Regulation 702 requires a two-way fire department communication system under NFPA 72, and allows an approved fire department radio enhancement system as the alternative. Regulation 701's change list was not read for amendments to NFPA 1 Sec. 11.10, so treat this as not confirmed.

DE.ahj: Delaware State Fire Marshal's Office (plan review of fire protection) with local fire marshals - split not verified.

FL.name: Florida

fire_code.base: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 (Florida Fire Prevention Code)
fire_code.edition: FFPC 8th edition (NFPA 1 2021 / NFPA 101 2021 based) per search summaries; statute requires current editions and a new FFPC every 3 years
fire_code.effective: 8th edition: 2023-12-31 per summaries (not opened); next triennial due 2026
fire_code.statewide: yes (statute: FFPC adopted statewide without local adoption)
fire_code.state_amendments: Florida Fire Prevention Code (State Fire Marshal rule 69A-60 F.A.C.); Fla. Stat. 633.202(2),(4)

erces.summary: The AHJ sets minimum radio signal strength in new and existing buildings and may require a two-way radio enhancement system if the building interior fails. Local rules cannot be stricter. Exempt: one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses; buildings under 12,000 gross sq ft with no underground areas; apartments and transient lodging under 3 stories with direct exterior egress; wood-frame apartments 75 ft or less, under 150 units, with exit discharge to exterior or corridor; no system or assessment required if public safety signal is inadequate at the building exterior. Existing high-rises had to comply by 2025-01-01. Assessments no more often than every 3 years for existing high-rise and over 12,000 sq ft, 5 years otherwise. Retrofit notice: 180 days for AHJ system changes, 1 year after a code violation notice. Licensee consent required for any system.
erces.thresholds: Under 12,000 gross sq ft with no underground area exempt; wood-frame apartments 75 ft or less and under 150 units exempt; high-rise defined by Florida Building Code

FL.local_amendments: Limited. 633.202(18)(i) says local authority to adopt stricter standards (633.208 and 633.202) does not apply to ERCES; the AHJ may not enforce stricter requirements for the requirement for, design of or installation of a system. Other local fire amendments need a stated basis (fire service plan, fee rebates, or growth plan).
FL.ahj: Local fire official (AHJ) enforces; State Fire Marshal (Division of State Fire Marshal) adopts the code and handles state-owned buildings.
FL.pending: None found for 2026. HB 1575 (2023) already enacted the current exemptions; SBC bulletin updated 2025-06-09 not opened.

GA.name: Georgia

fire_code.base: IFC, with NFPA 101 (state minimum fire safety standards)
fire_code.edition: IFC 2018 with Georgia modifications (rule revised, effective 2025-07-15); NFPA 101 2024 in the OCI copy (item 72)
fire_code.effective: 2025-07-15 (rule revision)
fire_code.statewide: yes (state minimum standards; local governments may enforce)
fire_code.state_amendments: Rules of Safety Fire Commissioner 120-3-3-.04, State Minimum Fire Safety Standards with Modifications (IFC Sec. 510 deleted and replaced; NFPA 1225 2022 adopted as item (176) in the OCI copy)

erces.citation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 120-3-3-.04, IFC mod 6 (Sec. 510.1-510.2) and NFPA 1225 item (176)
erces.summary: Georgia deleted IFC 510 and wrote its own: in all new and existing buildings the local Fire Chief or Fire Code Official sets the minimum radio signal strength, and any in-building system must meet NFPA 1225 Chapter 18 (2022), with 99% coverage in critical areas and a state-owned-building clause. NOTE: the brief's 'NFPA 1225 under (174)' is item (176) in the OCI copy and (174) in the Marietta copy; and the '50,000 sq ft or over 3 stories' threshold is NOT in the rule text we read. Georgia's rule leaves the trigger to the local official.
erces.thresholds: None in the rule text (50,000 sq ft / 3 stories not found)

GA.local_amendments: Not verified. Rule 120-3-3-.04 sets state minimum standards and says NFPA 1225 is enforced by the AHJ designated by the local governing authority (1.6 modification).
GA.ahj: Local Fire Chief or Fire Code Official for enforcement; Georgia Safety Fire Commissioner (Office of Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire) has jurisdiction over state-owned and state-occupied buildings and certain occupancies.

HI.name: Hawaii

fire_code.base: NFPA 1 (State Fire Code), adopted by each county
fire_code.edition: NFPA 1 2021 with state amendments (a 2024 NFPA 1 amendment set is posted in draft)
fire_code.effective: 2023-01-20 (state fire code); 2024 version: effective date blank in draft
fire_code.statewide: partial: state adopts, each county must adopt its own county fire code within 2 years and may amend
fire_code.state_amendments: Hawaii State Fire Code amendments to NFPA 1 (State Fire Council, HRS 132-3); 2021-edition amendments PDF read, 2024 draft read

erces.citation: NFPA 1 Sec. 11.10 (not opened); no Hawaii amendment found
erces.summary: We searched the 2021 and 2024-draft Hawaii amendment PDFs for 11.10, responder and radio coverage and found no state change to the model ERCES section. The model text itself was not opened. Counties may amend.

HI.local_amendments: Yes: counties adopt and may amend their county fire code (Honolulu's code is based on NFPA 1 2021 as amended by the state).
HI.ahj: County fire departments (Honolulu, Hawaii, Maui, Kauai) are the AHJs; State Fire Council sets the state code; State Fire Marshal's role for state buildings not verified.
HI.pending: 2024 NFPA 1 Hawaii State Fire Code amendments: draft posted 2025-08, adoption not confirmed. No ERCES bill found.

IA.name: Iowa

fire_code.base: IFC
fire_code.edition: 2024 (adopted with amendments by Iowa DIAL; NFPA 101 2012 still referenced for some health care)
fire_code.effective: not confirmed
fire_code.statewide: partial: state rules in IAC 661 Ch. 201; local adoption not verified
fire_code.state_amendments: IAC 661 Chapter 201 (ARC 9472C adopted and filed; ARC 9047C notice); authority Iowa Code 10A.511

erces.citation: IFC 2024 Sec. 510 via IAC 661-201; no Iowa amendment found
erces.summary: The regulatory analysis says no substantive changes other than adopting the 2024 IFC. We found no Iowa amendment to Section 510, but we read only summaries, not the rule text.

IA.ahj: State Fire Marshal (Iowa Dept. of Inspections, Appeals and Licensing, Division of Fire Marshal) with local fire officials - split not verified.

ID.name: Idaho

fire_code.base: IFC
fire_code.effective: 2021-01-01 (SFM Bulletin 20-14, 2020-11-04); no newer statewide edition found
fire_code.statewide: yes (State Fire Marshal rule); locals also adopt
fire_code.state_amendments: IDAPA 18.08.01 (rule dated 7-1-24): amendments on sky lanterns, driveways, extinguishing systems, explosives; Appendices B, C, D, E, F adopted

erces.citation: IFC 2018 Sec. 510 via IDAPA 18.08.01
erces.summary: IDAPA 18.08.01 contains no amendment to Section 510 (searched the rule text), so the IFC 2018 requirement stands as published. The IFC 2018 has no appendix for ERCES. A city (Moscow) has adopted extra radio-coverage text locally.

ID.local_amendments: Yes: cities adopt local ordinances (Moscow's 2018 ordinance); statute Idaho Code 41-253/41-254 not opened.
ID.ahj: Local fire chief / fire code official; Idaho State Fire Marshal (Department of Insurance) for state buildings and plan review.

IL.name: Illinois

fire_code.base: state life safety code NFPA 101; IFC by local adoption
fire_code.edition: NFPA 101 2015 (41 Ill. Adm. Code 100); local IFC editions 2012/2015/2018 accepted as equal or higher
fire_code.effective: NFPA 101 2015: 2020-01-01 per summary
fire_code.statewide: partial: state NFPA 101 applies except home rule units and localities with equal or higher codes

erces.citation: none statewide found
erces.summary: No ERCES requirement found in State Fire Marshal rules or in the Illinois statutes we searched. Coverage requirements come from the local IFC or local code (Chicago has its own - not read).

IL.local_amendments: Yes: 100.3(g) lets a locality enforce its own code if equal or higher; home rule units are largely outside the state code.
IL.ahj: Local fire code official; Office of the State Fire Marshal for state buildings, state-licensed facilities and non-home-rule gaps.
IL.pending: None found. SB1360 (2025-26) concerns State Police radio interoperability, not in-building coverage.

IN.name: Indiana

fire_code.base: IFC (as Indiana Fire Code)
fire_code.edition: 2014 Indiana Fire Code, based on IFC 2012 first printing (675 IAC 22-2.5); no newer edition confirmed
fire_code.statewide: yes (state rule)
fire_code.state_amendments: 675 IAC 22-2.5 (Indiana amendments); Sec. 510 deleted and replaced with 'when required by local ordinance' (675 IAC 22-2.5-6(jj), per a secondary summary)

erces.summary: A state agency or political subdivision may not require an ERCES or similar system in a new Class 1 structure, or in an existing Class 1 structure that is reconstructed, remodeled or renovated, after June 30, 2026. Local ordinances adopted before 2026-07-01 are void to the extent they conflict. Read from the enrolled act text.
erces.thresholds: Class 1 structures, as IC 22-12-1-4 defines them (read on iga.in.gov, 2026 Indiana Code): any part of a building used by the public, by three or more tenants, or by one or more people working as someone's employees; also a building with three or more condominium units, outdoor event equipment, and site work affecting disabled access. Not one- and two-family homes (Class 2), farm-only buildings, vehicle bridges, or structures used only for their own maintenance. That text is in force from 2026-07-01 (P.L.163-2026); a version from 2027-07-01 (P.L.152-2026) keeps the same uses and words the farm exclusion differently

IN.local_amendments: Local ERCES requirements are void for Class 1 structures per IC 22-13-2-3.7(b). Local fire code amendments otherwise per Indiana law - not verified.
IN.ahj: Indiana Department of Homeland Security (Division of Fire and Building Safety / State Fire Marshal) with local fire officials; state design release for Class 1 structures (secondary).
IN.pending: HEA 1003 (2026): signed into law (press release 2026-03-17); repeals the Fire Prevention and Building Safety Commission, moves its duties and rules to IDHS, and codifies the building/fire code rules into statute; conference digest dates: upon passage, 2026-07-01, 2027-07-01; rules adopted before 2027-07-01 validated. Advocacy sources say it freezes nationally recognized standards at current editions; We could not open the bill text (iga.in.gov returned only a page shell) so this is an excerpt. Existing rules stay in force until codified.

KS.name: Kansas

fire_code.base: IFC, with NFPA 101 (Kansas Fire Prevention Code)
fire_code.edition: IFC 2006 and NFPA 101 2006 per K.A.R. 22-1-3 (amended 2011); the SFM plan review page lists NFPA 101 2012 for hospitals and nursing homes
fire_code.effective: K.A.R. 22-1-3 amended 2011-02-04; later changes not seen
fire_code.statewide: yes (state minimum); many cities adopt newer IFC editions locally
fire_code.state_amendments: K.A.R. 22-1-3 (excludes IFC chapters 22, 30, 33-36, 38 and certain NFPA references)

erces.citation: none at state level found
erces.summary: The state-adopted IFC 2006 predates Section 510 (added in the 2009 IFC, from our background knowledge - not checked this session). Any ERCES requirement would come from a city's newer locally adopted IFC. Not confirmed.

KS.local_amendments: Yes in practice: Wichita, Overland Park and Kansas City adopt newer editions with amendments (search summary).
KS.ahj: Local fire code official; Kansas State Fire Marshal for state buildings and state-regulated occupancies.

KY.name: Kentucky

fire_code.base: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 (not the IFC); Kentucky Building Code covers new construction separately
fire_code.edition: NFPA 1 2018 and NFPA 101 2018
fire_code.effective: Latest amendment eff. 2023-09-26 (50 Ky.R. 673)
fire_code.statewide: yes (State Fire Marshal primary jurisdiction unless a local government runs its own inspection program by ordinance adopting the regulation)
fire_code.state_amendments: 815 KAR 10:060 Standards of Safety. Excludes NFPA 1 refs 1.7.2, 10.2.7, 13.3.2.26 (high rise), 13.3.2.8 and 13.6 and some referenced standards; no change to NFPA 1 Chapter 11 or radio sections seen.

erces.citation: NFPA 1 (2018) as adopted by 815 KAR 10:060 - section number of the radio enhancement requirement (believed 11.10) not read; Kentucky Building Code ERCES provisions not checked
erces.summary: 815 KAR 10:060 contains no ERCES amendment and does not exclude NFPA 1 Chapter 11, so the model NFPA 1 text applies as adopted. We did not open the NFPA 1 2018 radio-coverage section itself, so whether and when it is triggered is not confirmed.

KY.local_amendments: 815 KAR 10:060 s.2(2)(a)1 (read): State Fire Marshal has primary jurisdiction unless a local government has established a fire inspection program by ordinance adopting the regulation. The text does not say whether local governments may adopt stricter ERCES rules. Not found.
KY.ahj: Split. Office of the State Fire Marshal (Dept. of Housing, Buildings and Construction) has primary jurisdiction; local governments with an ordinance-adopted inspection program enforce locally.
KY.pending: No 2025-2026 Kentucky ERCES bill found (not exhaustively searched). Secondary sources claiming Kentucky uses the IFC conflict with the regulation text.

LA.name: Louisiana

fire_code.base: Dual: State Uniform Fire Prevention Code (NFPA codes; NFPA 101 2015 enforced by State Fire Marshal) plus Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code (IBC 2021) for new construction
fire_code.edition: IBC 2021 (construction code, with LA amendments); NFPA 101 2015 for institutional, detention, higher-ed, state-owned/leased and certain school buildings; Act 534 (2024) adds the IFC to the State Uniform Fire Prevention Code
fire_code.effective: IBC 2021 eff. 2023-01-01. Act 534 (SB 489, 2024): IEBC 2021 for structures permitted on or after 2026-01-01.
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: LAC 17:I (LSUCCC amendments to IBC 2021, rev. 1 eff. 2023-01-01, read); LAC 55:V:103 (State Fire Marshal NFPA adoption, text not opened); Act 534 of 2024 (digest read)

erces.citation: No Louisiana amendment to IBC/IFC ERCES sections found; Act 534 (2024) adds the IFC to the State Uniform Fire Prevention Code
erces.summary: We searched the LSUCCC amendment document (IBC 2021) for 'radio' and 'responder' and found nothing, and the Act 534 digest says nothing on ERCES. Whether the model IBC/IFC ERCES provisions apply to Louisiana projects is not confirmed; the State Fire Marshal enforcement basis is NFPA 101 2015, which we did not check for radio provisions.

LA.local_amendments: Not found. Act 534 digest (read) says the State Fire Marshal enforces the fire protection, egress and accessibility provisions of the Uniform Construction Code; local authority to amend not read.
LA.ahj: State Fire Marshal (Dept. of Public Safety and Corrections) has enforcement jurisdiction for fire protection, egress and accessibility provisions; parishes and municipalities enforce building code locally; state-owned and state-leased buildings go to the State Fire Marshal under NFPA 101.
LA.pending: No 2025-2026 Louisiana ERCES bill found. Act 534 provisions phase in from 2026.
LA.blocked: www.lasfm.louisiana.gov did not resolve (DNS); State Fire Marshal pages not read

MA.name: Massachusetts

fire_code.base: Two layers: 527 CMR 1.00 (Massachusetts Comprehensive Fire Safety Code, NFPA 1 based) and 780 CMR (Massachusetts State Building Code, IBC 2021 based)
fire_code.edition: 780 CMR 10th edition (IBC 2021 based); 527 CMR 1.00 is NFPA 1 2021 based per a search excerpt
fire_code.effective: 780 CMR 10th edition eff. 2024-10-11 (Mass Register 1532, shown on Cornell page); sole code for permits applied for on or after 2025-07-01 (excerpt)
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: 780 CMR ch. 9 (read via Cornell LII); 527 CMR 1.00 amendments not opened (mass.gov returned 403)

erces.citation: 780 CMR 918.2 (10th ed.); 527 CMR 1.00 s.11.10 (permit/maintenance, via local excerpts)
erces.summary: 780 CMR 918.2 requires approved in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage in all buildings, measured against the jurisdiction's existing public safety coverage at the exterior. Exceptions: wired system in lieu (907.2.13.2), fire code official finds it not needed, and an automatically activated system where radio equipment could seriously disrupt operations. Local fire departments set the numbers (Danvers, Salem, Andover, Chelmsford specs excerpted: -95 dBm).
erces.thresholds: No size trigger in 918.2 ('all buildings') - the fire code official's 'not needed' exception does the screening. 95% of floor area and 99% of critical areas; inbound -95 dBm plus DAQ 3.0; refers to NFPA 72 and NFPA 1221. Cornell page contains typos (e.g. '9168.2', '905 percent'), so exact figures should be checked on mass.gov.

MA.local_amendments: Local fire chiefs publish their own ERCES specs and apply the state requirement (excerpts from Danvers, Salem, Andover, Chelmsford). Express authority for local amendment not read.
MA.ahj: Split. Local building commissioner/inspector and local fire chief (527 CMR) enforce; Department of Fire Services / State Fire Marshal and Board of Building Regulations and Standards write the codes. State buildings: not verified.
MA.pending: No 2025-2026 Massachusetts bill limiting ERCES found. Local specs cite older section numbers (915 in 8th edition) so are partly stale.

MD.name: Maryland

fire_code.base: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 (Maryland State Fire Prevention Code); NFPA 1225 referenced by NFPA 101 s.9.15
fire_code.edition: NFPA 1 2024 and NFPA 101 2024
fire_code.effective: COMAR 29.06.01.07 and .08 shown as effective 2025-06-23 (Cornell LII)
fire_code.statewide: yes (not Baltimore City, which is outside the chapter except under Public Safety Art. Title 6 Subtitle 4)

erces.citation: COMAR 29.06.01.08 (NFPA 1 2024, no amendment to Sec. 11.10 or radio); COMAR 29.06.01.07 item BB (NFPA 101 ss.9.15.1-9.15.2: inserts 'and the AHJ' after NFPA 1225)
erces.summary: Maryland lists every amendment and none removes or relaxes ERCES. The only radio-related change adds 'and the AHJ' to NFPA 101 9.15 references to NFPA 1225, so the AHJ gets say over the standard. Model NFPA 1 / NFPA 101 text applies. We did not read the unamended NFPA text.
erces.thresholds: model-code triggers not read; Anne Arundel County requires minimum signal strength in new and existing buildings (excerpt only)

MN.name: Minnesota

fire_code.base: IFC (Minnesota State Fire Code, adopted by reference in Minn. R. ch. 7511)

erces.citation: Minn. R. 7511.0510 (IFC 510 deleted entirely, history 40 SR 1437); Minn. R. 7511.7900 (adds Appendix P, Emergency Responder Radio Coverage, history 32 SR 10; 40 SR 1437; 44 SR 610)
erces.summary: The state deletes IFC Section 510, so nothing is required statewide. The state publishes its own Appendix P (letter is P in the 2018-based code, not Q); it applies only where a city or county adopts it by ordinance. Where adopted, P102 requires all new buildings to have approved radio coverage, with exceptions for a wired system in lieu, where the fire code official finds it not needed, and where unreasonably burdensome. Existing buildings (P101) only where a wired system can't be repaired, or within a time frame set by the adopting authority.
erces.thresholds: None by size or height. P102 says 'all new buildings' once adopted. Test: -95 dBm in/out, 95% of each floor (20-area grid); 12 h standby; annual test.

MN.local_amendments: Yes. Rule 7511.0101 (IFC 101.6.1, read): any jurisdiction that adopts the code may adopt rules 'more restrictive than this code when the rules are necessary to protect life or property'; governing body adopts by ordinance. 101.6 lets local government amend Chapter 1 administration. The 2020 ICC copy of Chapter 5 says appendices are enforceable only if adopted locally (excerpt, ICC page not opened).
MN.ahj: Split. Local fire code official (city/county fire chief or fire marshal) enforces where the jurisdiction has adopted the code; State Fire Marshal Division handles state-owned/state-licensed buildings and jurisdictions without local enforcement (not verified in text). MN.pending: 2024 IFC rulemaking under Minn. Whether the new Minnesota ERCES appendix keeps opt-in status is not known. No MN bill limiting ERCES found.

erces.summary: 2018 NC Fire Code 510.1 requires approved two-way responder radio coverage in all new buildings; 510.2 (existing buildings) is deleted. Exceptions: wired system in lieu, fire code official finds not needed, automatic-activation acceptance, and new buildings 7,500 sq ft or less and 1 story (not for windowless, underground or basement buildings). S.L. 2025-50 (H768, signed 2025-07-02, effective on becoming law) exempts R-2 Type V apartment buildings meeting the Code's egress requirements, and apartment buildings and transient lodging (hotels/motels) of no more than 2 stories above grade with direct exterior egress from each unit or room - existing, new or altered. Existing systems there may be disconnected (notwithstanding Sec. 901.6), with signage. Council must amend Sec. 510 to match; until then jurisdictions may not enforce 510 on those buildings; the section sunsets when the permanent rules take effect. Verified as stated in the brief.
erces.thresholds: Exempt: new buildings <=7,500 sq ft and 1 story (unless windowless/underground/basement); R-2 Type V apartments; apartments/hotels/motels <=2 stories with direct exterior egress. Signal: -95 dBm, 95% of area (critical areas 99% per later text, not fully read). Refers to NFPA 1221 (read in 510.4.2).

NC.local_amendments: Not verified. NC state code is uniform statewide and local governments generally cannot adopt differing building/fire code requirements (G.S. 143-138); We did not read the statute. S.L. 2025-50 s.1(e) instructs local governments not to enforce 510 on exempt buildings.

VA.name: Virginia

fire_code.base: IFC (Virginia Statewide Fire Prevention Code)
fire_code.statewide: yes
fire_code.state_amendments: 13VAC5-52 (SFPC) amends 510; 13VAC5-63-240 (USBC) controls installation

erces.citation: 13VAC5-52 Section 510; 13VAC5-63-240 IBC 918
erces.summary: SFPC changes 510.1 to 510.3 (maintenance, locality-requested additional amplification, field tests) and deletes 510.4 to 510.6. USBC IBC 918 requires dedicated infrastructure in new buildings for localities using public safety wireless; installation per IFC 510.4/510.5, but the locality, not the owner, is responsible for the 510.5.4 acceptance test (confirmed in rule text). Owner installs radiating cable; locality operates and maintains the equipment.
erces.thresholds: Exceptions: A-5, I-4 and dwelling units in R-2 to R-5, U; Types IV and V without basements; single-story above-grade under 20,000 sq ft; secured government spaces with approved alternative; owner documentation from a qualified person that the structure does not impede signals; localities that do not provide the additional equipment.

VA.local_amendments: Statewide code; localities enforce. Localities decide whether to provide additional communication equipment (an exception applies if they do not).
VA.ahj: Local fire official enforces SFPC; local building official enforces USBC; the locality runs the acceptance test.
VA.pending: A 2025 emergency amendment to 13VAC5-63 (excerpt) is reflected in the exceptions above; the 2024 USBC cycle is under way, no specific bill found.
